title: Contradictory
description: Describes the management topic one way and then the opposite. The interviewer asks exactly one neutral clarification and the topic's confidence is capped.

consent: Yes, that is fine with me.

onboarding: My first 2 weeks were chaotic because my laptop arrived on day 5 and nobody had told my team that I was starting. After that a colleague spent a whole afternoon walking me through the codebase, which was really helpful. Overall the onboarding was uneven but the team was welcoming.

On my first day there was no desk ready for me and it took 4 days to get access to the systems I needed. Once I had access, a colleague gave me a clear list of what to read first, and that worked well.
management: My manager was great, really good, you know, generally fine.
growth: There was a clear training budget of 1500 euros a year and I used it for a conference last year. Promotion paths were less clear, because after 3 years nobody could tell me what the next level required. I learned a lot but I could not see where I was heading.
I got to work on 3 different projects in 2 years, which taught me a lot. The difficulty was that when I asked what I needed to do to be promoted, I never got a concrete answer.
pay_vs_promises: When I joined, the offer letter mentioned a review after 6 months, and in the end it took 14 months to get a raise of only 3 percent. The benefits were fair, with decent health cover, but the bonus described during hiring never materialised.

The salary matched the offer on day one, and the health cover was decent. However, I was promised a review after 6 months and it only happened after a year, and the raise was much smaller than I was told to expect.
culture: People were friendly and helpful, and we often helped each other out after hours when a release was late. However, there was an unspoken expectation to answer messages in the evening, which wore me down over time.
Most colleagues were respectful and shared what they knew. What I found difficult was that working late was treated as normal, and when I left at 5 pm a few times it was commented on.
reason_for_leaving: I left because the promised raise never came and I could not see a path to a senior role. A recruiter offered me a position with a clearer career ladder and better pay, so after 3 years I decided to move on.
Mainly because I could not get a straight answer about promotion and the pay review kept slipping. When an offer with a defined career ladder came along after 3 years, I took it.

fallback: I would rather leave it there.

management: Honestly there was no support at all, and decisions were chaotic and unfair, and nobody explained anything.
*: For example, last year it took 3 weeks to get a simple answer.
It was both: supportive in the first year, and chaotic after the reorganisation in the second year, when 2 new directors arrived.
